stem: A client receiving gastric enteral nutrition has a gastric residual volume of 350 mL and no nausea, vomiting, abdominal distention, or other signs of feeding intolerance. Which nursing interpretation is most appropriate?

options.A: A residual volume below 500 mL without other signs of intolerance should not by itself trigger stopping enteral nutrition; assess tolerance and follow agency policy.
options.B: Any gastric residual above 200 mL requires permanent discontinuation of enteral nutrition regardless of the client's clinical status.
options.C: The feeding rate should be doubled immediately to clear the residual volume more quickly.
options.D: Gastric residual volume is the only valid measure of enteral-feeding tolerance, so other gastrointestinal findings are unnecessary.

rationale: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals states that although gastric residual volumes of 200-500 mL have historically prompted interventions, current evidence does not support stopping enteral nutrition for GRVs less than 500 mL when there are no other signs of intolerance. Nurses should assess for symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, bloating, cramping, diarrhea, or constipation and follow agency policy. Therefore A is correct; the other options overstate or misuse the residual-volume finding.
educational_objective: Interpret gastric residual volume together with the client's clinical signs of enteral-feeding intolerance rather than using an isolated sub-500-mL value as an automatic stop criterion.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf — Open Resources for Nursing (Open RN)
source_version_date: Current Open RN edition available through NCBI; rechecked 2026-08-17
source_locator: Chapter 14 > enteral nutrition/aspiration-risk section: do not stop enteral nutrition for GRVs less than 500 mL in absence of other intolerance signs; follow agency policy; monitor for bloating, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, cramping, constipation
source_claim_supported: An isolated gastric residual volume below 500 mL without other signs of feeding intolerance should not automatically prompt stopping enteral nutrition; clinical tolerance and agency policy should guide management.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort, printed p.11/PDF p.15: Assist with nutrition and oral hydration; Provide care related to feeding and enteral tubes
blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — enteral-feeding tolerance and tube-feeding management
correction_summary: Replaced the vague 'unusually high residual' and facility-threshold-only answer with a concrete 350-mL scenario plus absence of intolerance. The corrected item uses the source-supported principle that GRV below 500 mL alone should not automatically stop enteral nutrition and explicitly incorporates clinical tolerance and agency policy.
